evidence: Proposed, not enacted. FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP) pp. 332, 338, 339, 346: 'In 2026 HRSA will be reorganized into the Agency [p.339: Administration] for a Healthy America to improve coordination of health resources for Americans.' Repeated for 2027 in the FY2027 Appendix (BUDGET-2027-APP) pp. 434, 439, 449. P.L. 119-75 keeps HRSA. Also FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)' -- names HRSA.

Not confirmed (owner, 2026-10-06). Proposed type, from explicit text: split_from -- FY2024 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2024-APP, HHS chapter granule BUDGET-2024-APP-1-10, PDF pp. 59 and 64): 'The 2024 Budget requests resources for the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) in a new account, separate from PHSSEF where funding has historically been appropriated.' P.L. 117-328 (FY2023) funds the preparedness programs under the Office of the Secretary's 'Public Health and Social Services Emergency Fund' heading (p.419); P.L. 118-47 (FY2024) has no such heading and an 'Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response' with this heading (p.211). Confirmed by the owner's test (2026-10-08), run on the first restated year: the FY2023 reports' FY2022 column prints no ASPR structure ('Total, PHSSEF' 3,199,678: H.Rept. 117-403 p.836; the FY2023 Senate draft p.419), so the FY2024 report's FY2023 column was used: S.Rept. 118-84 restates FY2023 as ASPR 3,629,677 (Research, Development, and Procurement 3,062,991 + Operations, Preparedness, and Emergency Response 566,686; pp.389-390) + a residual PHSSEF 137,892 (p.392) = 3,767,569 (thousands), exactly the FY2023 law's PHSSEF paragraphs (P.L. 117-328 div. H: $1,647,569,000 + $820,000,000 + $965,000,000 + $335,000,000 = $3,767,569,000). Through FY2023 ASPR's programs were funded within PHSSEF: P.L. 117-328 appropriates them under its PHSSEF heading (owner, 2026-10-09: Enacted follows the law; ASPR's FY2023 Enacted figures, S.Rept. 118-84's restatement, retired). Note: Funded within PHSSEF before FY2024. Cell note (ACC-HHS-ASPR-RDP FY2023 Enacted): S.Rept. 118-84 restates FY2023 in the FY2024 structure (ASPR separate from PHSSEF): 3,062,991 thousand (p.389).

Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.13 (PDF p.3), Environmental Health: 'National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS): $594.1 million'. Amount match: H.Rept. 119-271 p.344 FY 2026 Request, NIEHS 594,086 (thousands) = $594.1M rounded. The FY2027 request instead proposes moving NIEHS into CDC (a placement note on the account, not a relationship). P.L. 119-75 keeps NIEHS under NIH.

Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.14 (PDF p.4), Environmental Health: 'Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act (EEOICPA): $50.8 million in mandatory funding (post-sequester)'. Amount match, pre- vs post-sequester: H.Rept. 119-271 p.342 FY 2026 Request prints 55,358 (thousands), the appropriation before sequestration; 55,358 - 50,800 = 4,558 (8.2%) sequestered. The FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP p.333), AHA's proposed Environmental Health account (075-0386), appropriates the same '$55,358,000' for EEOICPA and shows, in $ millions for 2026: mandatory appropriation 55, permanently reduced -4, mandatory total 51 (= $50.8M rounded). P.L. 119-75 keeps it under CDC.

Proposed, not enacted (FY2019 President's Budget and House bill). The request moved the Strategic National Stockpile from CDC's 'Public Health Preparedness and Response' to PHSSEF/ASPR (H.Rept. 115-862 p.384: 575,000; CDC PHPR 800,000, p.363); H.R. 6470 did too ($710,000,000 under PHSSEF, p.93; H.Rept. 115-862 p.384). S. 3158 (p.57: $1,470,000,000, of which $610,000,000 for the SNS) and P.L. 115-245 (p.93: $1,465,200,000, of which $610,000,000) kept it in CDC. Recorded by the owner's rule (2026-10-09): stages of one year with different structures. Through FY2019 the law appropriated it to CDC (P.L. 115-245 p.93).
